name: issue_829_manual_origin_unclosed_grace_loop
description: A default-duration WHF-on (no timer selected) whose grace expires while the fan is still physically running must not have its eventual real off, hours later, misread as a fresh unexplained override that re-locks CA out of the fan (Issue #829)
notes: Occupant impact if this regresses: turning the whole-house fan on for a while with no
timer -- a completely ordinary interaction -- can trigger a loop where CA silently
reactivates the fan on its own after the override's grace expires, then, whenever that
reactivated run ends (minutes to hours later, not seconds), re-locks itself out of the
fan for a brand-new full manual_grace_seconds window as if the user had just done
something fresh and unexplained. Confirmed live over two nights (2026-09-01 and
2026-09-02/03): the same WHF session's real end kept restarting a fresh 180-minute
grace every time CA had quietly re-adopted it, forever unable to settle into 'the user
already told us they don't want this fan on right now'.
This scenario reproduces the exact handoff moment end-to-end through the real
coordinator, including the parts a unit test can't reach (the real grace timer,
the real _on_grace_expired()/_post_grace_fan_check_callback() dispatch, the real
nat-vent reactivation gate): the WHF is turned on externally with no RF timer
involved (external_fan_state_change, state=on -- routes through the real
coordinator._async_fan_entity_changed -> handle_fan_manual_override(), arming a
manual_grace_seconds-duration override with no _fan_remote_timer_hours, exactly the
'no timer selected on the device' case the issue reports). A window opens shortly
before the 3h grace expires. At expiry, with the sensor still open, production's
real _on_grace_expired() takes its 're-pause, sensor still open' branch and schedules
_re_pause_for_open_sensor(), which independently re-evaluates nat-vent eligibility
and reactivates the fan on CA's own initiative (nat_vent_reactivated_while_paused) --
the exact live moment _fan_manual_origin_unclosed must be set. As observed live, this
run reached the reactivation leg (_re_pause_for_open_sensor()) rather than the
override-clear-while-still-running leg (clear_fan_override()) -- both call sites set
the same marker via the same mechanism, so this still exercises the fix's real
arming behavior through the full, unmodified production stack.
Closing the loop with a subsequent real fan-off and confirming no fresh grace starts
is proven precisely at the unit level instead
(tests/test_whole_house_fan_hvac_suppression.py::TestFanManualOriginUnclosed) --
attempts to script a second synthetic external_fan_state_change late in this same
scenario landed inside another production reconcile cycle's own fan-state handling
(visible in the decision timeline as fan_running_untracked/fan_untracked_cleared
around the same grace-expiry tick) and could not be made to reliably assert a single
specific downstream event without over-fitting to that cycle's exact internal timing
-- a known limitation of this event-driven harness for very tightly-spaced synthetic
events, not evidence against the fix. The unit tests drive on_fan_turned_off()
directly with the marker pre-set, proving its consuming behavior deterministically.
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: if _re_pause_for_open_sensor()'s reactivation branch
stopped setting _fan_manual_origin_unclosed, this scenario would still show
nat_vent_reactivated_while_paused firing (proving the reactivation itself is
unaffected) -- the marker's own consuming effect is what the unit-level tests
verify deterministically; this scenario's job is proving the real production
grace-expiry/reconcile/reactivation machinery actually reaches the arming call
site under realistic conditions, not a hand-picked unit-test precondition.
(b) Docs-production alignment: docs/grace-periods-spec.md's new
'Manual-Origin Unclosed Marker (Issue #829)' section documents this exact mechanism
and was written and verified against this same incident trace.
(c) User outcome: verified above in the occupant-impact note.

events.note: Evening: indoor=73F, outdoor=60F -- favorable for nat-vent (outdoor well below indoor, above comfort_heat).

Seed the fan_entity's initial baseline state -- the first-ever state write on an entity has no old_state to diff against, so the listener would otherwise never dispatch. Matches the existing manual_whf_on_suppresses_hvac.json golden scenario's pattern.

User turns the WHF on directly (no RF remote timer entity involved, and no window open yet -- fan was genuinely OFF) -- the exact 'no timer selected on the device' case. Routes through the real coordinator listener to handle_fan_manual_override(), arming a manual_grace_seconds (10800s / 3h) override with no _fan_remote_timer_hours.
Window opens shortly before the 3h override grace expires (20:37) -- matches the live incident, where the fan kept running under nat-vent's identity once the grace cleared.

Just after the 3h grace expiry (20:37): still favorable for nat-vent -- the real production _on_grace_expired()/_re_pause_for_open_sensor() path reactivates the fan on CA's own initiative while the sensor stays open (nat_vent_reactivated_while_paused), the exact live moment _fan_manual_origin_unclosed must be armed.

assertions.reason: The initial no-timer WHF-on must still be correctly detected and armed as a manual override -- proves the scenario's setup actually exercises the real override path this fix builds on, not a no-op.
The grace-expiry reactivation this fix's marker is armed against must genuinely happen through the real production gate (not assumed) -- proves the scenario reaches the code path it claims to.

Issue #829's fix: the real production _re_pause_for_open_sensor() reactivation branch must arm _fan_manual_origin_unclosed on this handoff -- proving the marker is set by actual production control flow (grace timer, reconcile callback, reactivation gate all real), not only by a unit test's hand-set precondition.

verdict.summary: A default-duration (no-timer) WHF-on whose grace expires while the fan is still running, and is then reactivated by CA's own grace-expiry logic, correctly arms the manual-origin-unclosed marker so its eventual real off is not misread as a fresh override (Issue #829)
verdict.observed_behavior: WHF turned on externally (manual override armed, no RF timer) -> sensor opens -> 3h later grace expires, sensor still open -> real production _re_pause_for_open_sensor() reactivates nat-vent on its own initiative -> _fan_manual_origin_unclosed is armed
verdict.expected_behavior: CA's own grace-expiry reactivation of a still-manually-originated fan session marks provenance so a later real off is recognized as closing that session, never as a fresh unexplained override -- the marker's consuming behavior is proven deterministically in tests/test_whole_house_fan_hvac_suppression.py::TestFanManualOriginUnclosed
